title: Popular Method books demand frequent bows and genuflections to Mary privately and in church—Alexis de Salo’s program
source_text: XXXVI. Praecipue vero libri illi vulgares, quos Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores & Rectores in manus plebis tradunt, Beatae Virginis adorationem internam & externam vehementer commendant; & a suis devotis exigunt, ut crebris corporis inclinationibus, & genuflexionibus suam erga sanctam Virginem reverentiam testentur, tam domi privatim, quam in Ecclesiis publice. Id speciatim videre est in Methodo colendae & honorandae Virginis, quam Italice edidit Alexis de Salo Capucinus, & quae postea fuit in Gallicam linguam versa & saepius impressa cum pluribus Doctorum approbationibus. Etenim author ille in praefatione testatur scopum suum esse docere multos devotos & egregios modos reverendi & adorandi cum profundissimis, ut loquitur reverentiis, id est, corporis inclinationibus, seu genuflexionibus, Reginam coelorum heram atque Dominam nostram. Et postea pollicetur primo se ostensurum adorationum talium praestantiam. Secundo quam sint Sanctae Virgini gratae. Tertio se quatuor rationibus evicturum dignissimam illam esse quae adoretur. Denique se acturum de ratione qua istae adorationes, seu genuflexiones sint, ad praxim redigendae, & devote fieri possint tam interne quam externe.
pass_a_gloss: But especially those vulgar books which the Doctors and Rulers of the Roman Church put into the people’s hands vehemently commend the interior and exterior adoration of the Blessed Virgin; and from their devout they exact that by frequent inclinations of the body and genuflections they testify their reverence toward the holy Virgin, both privately at home and publicly in the Churches. That is especially to be seen in the Method of cultivating and honoring the Virgin, which Alexis de Salo the Capuchin published in Italian, and which afterward was turned into the French tongue and often printed with many Doctors’ approbations. For that author in the preface testifies that his aim is to teach many devout and excellent modes of revering and adoring with the most profound reverences, as he speaks—that is, inclinations of the body, or genuflections—the Queen of heaven, our Lady and Mistress. And afterward he promises first that he will show the excellence of such adorations. Second how grateful they are to the Holy Virgin. Third that by four reasons he will prove her most worthy to be adored. Finally that he will treat of the way by which those adorations, or genuflections, are to be reduced to practice, and can devoutly be done both inwardly and outwardly.
pass_b_english: Handbooks pressed on the people push Marian adoration—bows and genuflections at home and in church.
Alexis de Salo’s approved Method trains deep reverences to the Queen of heaven and maps them into practice.
